title: Prove a paragraph quoting the heading no longer moves the section
action: Add tests for D1 and prove them red then green. (1) #[cfg(test)] unit tests in heading_section.rs: a paragraph quoting the heading before the real heading line does not move the section; a longer line that starts with the heading text does not match; CRLF heading line matches; no heading line gives None; section ends at the next '## ' line. (2) A #[cfg(test)] test in ownership.rs whose name contains heading_section: parse_agents_rule_homes on a body whose earlier paragraph quotes '## AGENTS.md rule homes' and whose real section holds one rule row returns exactly that row. (3) A test in tests/rule_index_parity.rs: rule_homes_section on a text with a quoting paragraph first returns the real section. Prove red: temporarily swap the helper body to a first-occurrence find, run the new tests and keep the failing output, then restore the helper byte for byte and run them green. Write no code comments. Do not edit production behavior.
